title: World Builder roadmap: spa replacement, small college campus, and narrative notebook worlds
robert_direction: Keep Robert updated on spa, Avatar Builder, World Builder, Kira body/movement, and TARDIS progress.

Finish a good standalone legal spa first. Keep the spa separate for now and leave the Home World former strip-mall site visually empty; preserve the old procedural source behind an explicit restore switch.
After the spa, prepare a small college campus plan with dorms, classrooms, labs, offices, a memorial union/student union, a college store, restaurants, places to eat, and places to relax.
Do not add the college campus to Home World until Robert upgrades to the 64 GB RAM kit.
Use notebook worlds for large places, book worlds, movie worlds, memory reconstructions, and separate worlds like Paris. Home World should remain a livable home base.

phase_order.goal: Create a realistic, walkable, legal day spa where Kira or another resident can talk with the Avatar Builder and request approved appearance or age-up changes.
approval_gate: Must include real front door, working interior doors, connected walls, clear route paths, and no hidden doorway blockers.
Must include an Avatar Builder room or station with talk-button interaction.
Must remain staged only until Robert reviews and approves it.
phase_order.home_world_action_after_approval: Keep the spa in legal_day_spa_notebook_world while the system has 32GB RAM. Reconsider a Home World placement only after 64GB is verified, a supervised multi-hour combined soak passes, all spa gates pass, and Robert explicitly approves the placement.

phase_order.goal: Keep the former strip-mall site visually empty by default without deleting the legacy source or placing the spa there.
notes: The current strip mall has navigation and blocked-door problems.
Default Home World startup skips the legacy meshes, colliders, doors, interaction zones, sign textures, and nested legacy spa suite.
The legacy source can be restored explicitly with ?stripMall=1 for comparison or recovery.
The Legal Day Spa remains a separate notebook world; emptying this site is not approval to transfer it.
Robotics and programming/AI labs should move to the future college campus.
Public-facing offices can be redesigned later as separate buildings if still wanted.

phase_order.goal: Build a small college-like campus for learning, expert offices, labs, dorm life, food, and memory reconstruction staging.
required_areas: lounges and outdoor places to relax
safe walking paths and clear building entrances
memory_reconstruction_use: When Kira, Lisa, Robert, or another resident wants to strengthen a college memory, the system can create a temporary reconstruction branch.
The reconstruction should copy only the needed memory context into the temporary scene and keep the original memory record intact.
Residents may watch the memory, relive it, or discuss it afterward, but the world must label reconstruction confidence when details are uncertain.
approval_gate: Do not place in Home World until Robert confirms the 64 GB RAM kit is installed and stable.
Build and review as a separate staged notebook world or TARDIS review bay first.

phase_order.goal: Create separate notebook worlds for places from books, movies, shows, and history so residents can watch or join reconstructed scenes.
examples_from_robert: 11/22/63: Jake Epping driving through Derry, Maine
operating_rules: Do not merge these worlds into Home World.
Use the TARDIS as the gateway and review area.

If a place exists in both a book and movie, local legally provided books/scripts/images/models may guide the scene, while movie actors or models can help create temporary avatar references only when allowed.
Scenes should be reconstructed from scene beats, summaries, and visual references, not by dumping or copying long copyrighted text.
Residents can watch the scene unfold or join the action in a branch timeline.
Branch timelines must be clearly marked so residents know whether they are observing, reenacting, or changing a temporary branch.
world_builder_requirements: Scan approved local source materials and make a source-confidence map.
Build environment first, then characters, then scene actions.
Generate a reviewable preview before live use.
Ask for approval when details are uncertain or when a scene may need special handling.

phase_order.goal: Use Marinette's bakery/home and nearby park as a Paris notebook-world source-evidence and floor-by-floor construction test.
approval_gate: Keep it as a Paris notebook-world draft, not Home World content.
Place the bakery/home beside the park according to Robert's corrected fictional-real map, not at the old Boris Lume/Montmartre seed.
Start with source audit, park/fountains/trees, and bakery exterior.
Build the home one floor at a time.
Trust pictures from the show over the fan blueprint; use the blueprint only to help with rough floor order and scale.
Move Marinette to her bedroom only after Robert approves the room, the avatar is usable, and the 64 GB RAM plan is ready.

update_policy.report_format: Short progress updates while running; final reports should list what improved, what failed, and what is still blocked.
do_not_claim_success_until: Robert can visually identify the result without labels.
Doors, routes, collision, and scale pass a practical walkthrough.
Kira/Lisa body actions match the world state instead of narrating impossible actions.
Preview artifacts include real models or runtime walkthroughs, not JSON-only proof.
